The lead-in exists to absorb key-up drift. Spec 2.8 (line 311) says receivers 'should take the starting state from the last 8 s of the lead-in'. An L1 A1 window starting at -10.5 s therefore includes the chirp. The measured +5 dB used clean tones, so start the window near -8.5 s, or measure with a simulated key-up chirp, before F1 is made the default. Inferred.

Moving the front-end cutoff is an alternative to R1/O19. With firwin(255, 1250 Hz) the FE is -6 dB at 250 and 2750 Hz and is flat only from 310 to 2690 Hz (measured), so both the noise bins and a 300 Hz CE carrier's own lower sideband (274 Hz, about -2 dB) sit on the skirt. Raising the cutoff about 50 Hz, or lengthening the filter, would put 300-2700 Hz inside the flat region. That fixes the signal and the noise together, but it changes every CE result, so it needs a flag or Jeff's OK. Inferred, not measured.

R7 and O1 interact. Rule 2 decodes once per near provisional cluster for every headerless pass, under the listener lock (associate.py:274-292; live.py:1303). Any larger list size, or more junk clusters (C1/O7), multiplies a 14.6 ms decode across a growing store. Do O1(c), associate outside the lock, before R7.

Existing precedents can be reused. drop_band_owned (acquire.py:1498-1519) already implements the L own-band rule, with its timing window, for preamble hits, and drop_symbol_rate_aliases handles CE's +-1/T. O2, L7(b) and D3 should extend those functions rather than add a third geometric rule.

CE's fading header is bounded by tracking. Spec 5.1: gate V fails on 14 of 16 passes at -28 dB moderate, and both copies decode at -26.9 dB moderate against -30.3 dB steady. That makes C2's timing fixes, behind a flag, the better-supported CE header lever than R7's list size, which helps mostly on steady paths.

verdicts.corrections: (1) The fallback is described wrongly. If a neighbour empties one side, sel is not empty, so the skirt side is used on its own. With no neighbour at all, the median is taken over both sides together, and it is still biased when one side sits in the skirt. The quieter-side min fires only when both sides are excluded (frontend.py:334-345). (2) Dividing every bin by |H_FE|^2 is NOT bit-identical mid-band. Measured: the passband ripple is 2.5e-4 dB over 500-2500 Hz. To keep mid-band bit-identical, touch only bins where |H| is below -0.01 dB (below 324 or above 2676 Hz, measured), or mask bins below -0.1 dB (310/2690 Hz). Then only channels centred below about 444 Hz or above about 2556 Hz change. (3) A rig's SSB filter rolls off at the same edges, and an FE-only correction cannot know about it. Near an edge, prefer the inward side or the log-average of the two sides (exact for a slope linear in dB), never the min. (4) There is a second caller: acquire.lead_in_span (acquire.py:965-968) calls noise_psd with no exclusions. At an edge it reads a low sigma2, inflates the lead-in Z, and can claim a lead-in on CE preamble hits that was never sent. Fix both callers. (5) It is more urgent than ranked: docs/qrss/60m.md:17-18 recommends audio offsets of 300-1900 Hz, so the recommended low end sits right in the failing zone. The seam exists: ChanCapture.noise_psd_at already knows mix_audio_hz (track.py:186-193).

(a) A hint that A2 fails today is put in `hinted` (acquire.py:1648-1651) and becomes a gate-V candidate at the finish, about a minute each in the 12-candidate / 180 s budget. (b) store.due hints only missing later segments g > k (store.py:393-417), so a repeat of the same segment, the main multi-pass case, is never hinted today. That makes R3 more valuable than ranked. At the spec's 30 Hz L spacing, occupied bands (about 22 Hz plus a margin) leave gaps of only about 5-8 Hz per 30 Hz. Even per-waveform exclusion then leaves almost no clean bin 85-120 Hz away, so in a dense band the fallback decides the result. Use the median of unoccupied gap bins across the band, and note that A1's band-wide CFAR median is itself biased once more than half the band is occupied (inferred). Plumbing: exclude_hz carries bare centres through channel_for, ChanCapture.exclude_hz and noise_psd (receiver.py:176-198, track.py:168-193). Per-waveform widths need (centre, half-width) pairs, and lead_in_span (acquire.py:967) needs them too. Medium cost, not small. The fallback change touches CE wherever it fires, so it needs a flag.

Make the fix bit-identical whenever there is no strong L signal. Notch only verified strong L lines (above -6 dB, which A1 finds trivially on the un-normalised FE) before the running median, and leave normalise (frontend.py:168-208) unchanged otherwise. CE is constant envelope and cannot cause this, so the STFT bin-median variant would change every CE result in exchange for a fix to an L-only problem. capture_prepare normalises before acquisition runs (live.py:298-300), so the order needs a cheap A1 pre-pass. Medium cost.

Insight 18 (association is quadratic): resolve_provisional runs on every rule-1 and rule-2 attach and reloads each accumulator once per cluster (associate.py:152-164, 376-392). Rule-3 and rule-4 changes do not trigger it, so an incremental version needs a dirty set, not just 'the pair that changed'.

Insight 8 (band-edge SNR): the numbers check out (computed: FE flat to 0.01 dB from 324 to 2676 Hz and to 0.1 dB from 310 to 2690; -1.4 dB at 280 Hz, -6.0 at 250, -29.6 at 200). Three additions. A real rig's SSB filter skirt adds the same bias, which no FE-only correction removes. The recommended 60 m offsets (docs/qrss/60m.md:17-18, 300-1900 Hz) start inside the failing zone. And acquire.lead_in_span uses the same floor with no exclusions.

Insight 18 also quotes store.due as predicting later passes 'for the same waveform at the same frequency'. It predicts only missing later segments g > k (store.py:393-417), never a repeat of a segment already held, which is the most common multi-pass case. That is why remembered-frequency hints (R3) are worth more than they look.

The header list size is not a CPU question. Measured, list 32 costs about 1.4x list 8 per attempt (33-36 against 24-26 ms) and gains about 0.3 dB on a steady channel (opt/verify_feas/m1_list.py), so any insight that treats list size as a CPU trade should be dropped.

On CE bit-identity: several items marked 'no CE change' change CE results on the joint path only. Extra L lines and hints (L1, L6, L7, R3) share the 12-candidate / 180 s finish budget with CE, and O5 and O6 add or keep CE passes. --just-ce stays bit for bit, but the default listener's CE output can move in busy slots.
missing: Re-receive a stored pass with its header known (round B) once association supplies that header, on both waveforms. em.rereceive(p, None, hdr) already does exactly that for CE (em.py:270-345), Store.update_pass exists (test_p1_update_pass_rebuilds), and each pass keeps its 250 Hz capture. Yet the listener never calls it: live.py imports nothing from em, and EM runs only via qrss_decode.py:177-181. Measured round-B gains: L +1.0 dB at -12 dB and +1.8 at -6, CE +0.8 at -12, and +0.1-0.5 dB (slope-corrected) at -24/-28. Every pass whose header decoded by soft combination or from a later pass keeps its round-A latents today. Cost: one track per such pass (about 6-7 s on FULL) in the idle finish child; CE stored z/w change, so it needs a flag; L needs L5's port first.

acquire.lead_in_span takes its sigma2 from frontend.noise_psd with no neighbour exclusion (acquire.py:965-968). A neighbour 85-120 Hz away raises the floor and can hide a real lead-in, and at a band edge the skirt lowers it and can claim a lead-in that was never sent. lead_in_s feeds keyed_from in the tracker's templates, so this touches CE preamble hits too. Fix it together with R1 and R4 (inferred, not measured).

Order the work by CPU. The finish is one child process at nice 5 (live.py:359-430), joint listening already costs +64%, and the L acquisition additions (R3, L1, L3, L6, L7) each add A2 or A3 work per slot. Land the CPU items (O2, O3, O8, O9, O15, O17) first, so a slot's finish stays well inside its 900 s cadence on laptop-class hardware (inferred).

Hints could also carry each station's measured drift. CarrierCandidate takes drift_hz_per_min, and track.report already fits it (drift_hz_per_min = line[0]*60), but _hints passes only f (live.py:1191-1223). For a rig that warms up the same way at every key-up (KC2G's +0.030 Hz/min, tentative), A2's fixed-line rotation would then start on the right slope (inferred).

Treat waveform_l as a format freeze point. d357ec8 is only on origin/waveform_l, pushed 2026-10-12, and the app on that branch already offers L transmit (native/gui/qrss_tx.cpp:33-34, 155-157). Until the F-batch (F2-F6) is decided, the branch should say plainly that L must not go on the air; otherwise the 'free now' window closes silently the first time someone keys it.

verdicts.corrections: MSE-based 'raw vs rescaled' latent SNR overstates the decoder-level cost. If k comes from |u_hat| (as the item says), w scales as 1/k^2 while z scales as k, so z*w is (w0/k)(a+n): the over-scaled pass is down-weighted automatically, and mean(w*e^2) stays honest. Combining the four measured round-A passes (k 0.83/1.02/1.49/0.99) with those weights loses (sum 1/k)^2/(N sum 1/k^2), which is -0.16 dB against ideal, with an essentially unbiased scale (0.996). After round B (k 1.00/1.04/1.23) the loss is -0.04 dB. Polar SC/SCL decisions are nearly invariant to a common LLR scale, so the '1.2x overconfident' point matters only relative to other passes in a sum. L5's round B already removes most of the spread (23% max against 49%).
verdicts.revised_gain: About 0.05-0.2 dB in multi-pass accumulation, about 0.05 dB once passes are round B. Single-pass decoder effect unmeasured, probably small (inferred, computed from the measured k values).

insight_corrections: 'A3 at the slot end reaches about -30 dB on L_FULL' is conservative. Measured (opt/verify-gain/m1_a3_lfull.py): 5/5 at -30 dB steady (p 5.6e-6 to 2.3e-4 against TBD_PFA 1e-3), 5/5 at -30 quiet (p 7e-8 to 2.6e-6), 5/5 at -28 quiet, 0/5 at -32 steady, where no hit was returned at all. The blind cliff is about -31 dB, and quiet fading reads slightly stronger than steady (z 55-57 against 52-54 at -30).

Insight 2 ('L's realised multi-pass gain depends on hints finding nearly every repeat') is wrong at the 16-pass good point. The finish's blind A3 found every L_FULL pass at -30 dB on steady and quiet, against the -29.6 dB per-pass target. Detection binds only deeper: the 32/64-pass good points (-32.3/-34.9) and the 16-pass usable/recognizable points (-34.3/-37.7). 'Combining works: 8 passes at -20 dB combine to the ideal 9 dB' is a CE measurement (e2e-results.md, run 2026-10-09 before the L receiver existed); L multi-pass combining has not been run end to end.

'L -29.6 / CE -26.4 after 16 passes' are spec model figures (sims/l_spread.py; spec 6.3/6.6). The model iterates EM-aided tracking to convergence (spec 6.4: 'many weak passes bootstrap each other through EM'). CE's -26.4 was confirmed in P3, but with the nominal frequency and timing handed to the receiver (README.md:805-809). L's figure is unmeasured and leans on a data-aided reference (20% -> 66%) that L's receiver does not have (EM is CE-only) and that measured small wherever tried. It is probably optimistic for L (inferred).

'For L the binding stage has moved from gate V to A1 and A3' needs splitting by path. For stored passes with at least half the slot heard (live.py:341-344), A1 is not binding: A3 is, at about -31 dB. A1 binds only for live tiles and in the heard < 0.5 finish branch (live.py:345-357). So the lead-in's '5 dB' is a live figure; for stored passes it is about 1.5-2 dB.

The lead-in A1 measurements used a drift-free lead-in tone. Spec 2.8's stated reason for the lead-in is a transmitter that drifts when it keys up, which A1's linear +-3 Hz/min drift cells match only partly. Real-rig gains will be smaller (inferred).

'A3's pilot-only emission is about 6 dB behind CE's' overstates how pilot-only it is. At -30 dB steady the best A3 path ran 3.3-16.1 Hz below the pilot, in the data band, in 5 of 5 trials, and the pilot-anchored re-path recovered the pilot within 0.23 Hz (m1). A3 already uses data-band lumps; an L-matched emission adds about 2-2.5 dB, not the full 6.

'Both refine_timing flaws showed up only under L's weaker references' is no longer true. Measured on CE SHORT at -27 dB (opt/verify-gain/m3_ce_timing.py, 9 seeds): from a 0.15 T start CE's refine_timing corrected 0 of 18. 14 stayed exactly at 0.150 T (Newton breaks on a non-PD Hessian, track.py:1257) and 4 walked off to 0.20-0.28 T, a mean 0.46 dB latent loss (max 1.47 dB). The flaw is live on CE at its multi-pass operating SNR. Whether it bites on FULL frames is unmeasured.

'The AGC follows L's envelope above -6 dB' needs a size attached, and the size is small. Measured gain modulation (opt/verify-gain/m2_agc_xmod.py) is 3.95% rms at -6 dB, 6.8% at 0, 15.4% at +10 and 20.4% at +20 dB. That caps every other signal's SINR at 28.1, 23.4, 16.3 and 13.8 dB: irrelevant to weak neighbours at any operating threshold.

'L's header is probably deeper than its -27 dB estimate' holds for steady paths only. On fading, CE's header is tracking-bound (-29.0 quiet, -26.9 moderate), and L's tracking is weaker, so L's fading header is plausibly no better than CE's.

'Erasure costs far more... argues for sending the 2,200 never-sent latents (+0.3 dB at the good level)': the +0.3 dB is SNR-equivalent, about +0.1 dB PSNR net (decoder-measurements.md:84-91: +0.15-0.19 dB PSNR gross minus 0.18 dB of energy), and nothing at usable or below, where deep multi-pass operates. F7's '+0.2 to +0.3 dB PSNR' repeats that unit error.

'SNR2500 reads 0.3-0.9 dB low... field figures probably pessimistic' comes from CE mid-band runs only. Near the band edges the same estimator reads up to 8.4 dB high (R1), so the sign depends on where the signal sits.

'L buys bandwidth, not dB, at a fixed peak' and F5(b) pull in opposite directions. waveform-l.md argues L is for heat-limited rigs, where its 3.2 dB average-power edge is the point, and for those stations F5(b)'s harder clipping costs 0.1-0.4 dB.

For CE it already binds: quiet -34 dB gives Z_ref about 4 at the true timing, 0/10 found (README.md:866-869). Late joins and restarts are where live acquisition decides the stored pass. With less than half the slot heard, the finish receives only live detections and hints (live.py:345-357), so L's live A1 limit (about -26 dB) applies there. How often listeners join late (restarts, recovery after outages, O13/O14) should decide how much live-only acquisition work (L6, L7) is worth.
